messages.text:
hello, Sarah, i've got a problem!

 My Nexus shuts down with a regulator overvoltage fault.  firmware
is  BitLuck nexus.v1.0.4.4,  Harlo was never written to it because my grok
bot said the only Harlo file with a similar name would program the wrong
regulator, hardware was not modified.  It ran for a couple of days at 440
MHz and 950 mV, about 140 W, with the board near 60°C, never exceeding
temperature limits, It failed at 425 MHz and 930 mV at 132W.

The miner was hashing normally. It now stops as soon as it starts. The
display shows either of these:

• VOLTAGE PROTECTION, Guru Meditation #····
• VREG OVERHEATED, Guru Meditation #····

It seems the 12 V input is healthy. At the moment of the fault the miner
measures 12.09 V

A USB serial log of the boot shows the controller finds the TPS53647, sets
4 phases, and commands 0.93 V at 425 MHz. The four chips accept the clock.
Within a fraction of a second the regulator reports:
Searched the web · Nexus S1 miner "VOLTAGE PROTECTION" Guru Meditation TPS53647
Searched the web · BitLuck Nexus firmware "VREG OVERHEATED" error TPS53647
Searched the web · harlolabs.com Harlo OS firmware Nexus S1 download
Handed to the team · Needs JD's read on the TPS53647 fault codes for BitLuck 1.0.4.4 (#···· / #44

Hi Fabio,

I am Hal, I look after the hardware side here, and Sarah passed your message to me. Good news on the parcel, sorry the unit is giving you trouble now.

From what you describe, the controller side of the board is healthy: it boots, finds the TPS53647, sets 4 phases and commands 0.93 V, and the four chips accept the clock. The fault happens the instant the core rail comes up, and it happens at a lower frequency, voltage and wattage than the unit already ran stably for two days. A 12 V rail sitting at 12.09 V during the fault also looks fine. That pattern points at the core voltage regulator itself rather than at your settings or your tuning.

Two things I want to be straight about. First, your decision not to write Harlo OS was the right one: the Nexus S1 is not on the Harlo flasher model list today, so stay on BitLuck nexus.v1.0.4.4 and do not load a profile built for another board. Second, I will not invent a meaning for #···· and #····. I could not find those two values documented for BitLuck 1.0.4.4. The closest documented case I can read is a VREG Overheated panic on an ESP-Miner board where the regulator reported an impossible internal temperature at the exact moment core voltage was enabled and the firmware cut the rail about 20 ms later; the person who reported it concluded it was not a firmware problem. Same shape as yours, different firmware family, so I treat it as a hint, not an answer.

Your email was cut off right at the sentence that matters, "Within a fraction of a second the regulator reports:", and then it ends. Please send me the rest of that serial log, from the TPS53647 detection down to the panic, as text or a screenshot. Any vr-temp or vr-fault line in there is the deciding evidence.

While you wait, three things. Please stop power cycling it repeatedly and do not raise the voltage to try to push it through, because each retry is another inrush into a regulator that is already complaining. If you happen to have another known good 12 V supply rated well above the unit's draw, around 12 V 15 A or more, try it once and tell me if the behaviour changes; a very brief droop during inrush produces exactly this code and a multimeter reading at steady state cannot see it. And send me a clear photo of the serial number label on the unit. If at any point you notice a burning smell, a hot connector or any mark on the board, unplug it and leave it unplugged.

I have put the full detail in front of JD, our hardware lead, with the model, firmware, your settings and both codes. He picks it up today from 10am Eastern and the answer comes back to you here in this thread. If you want a faster read in the meantime, JD and a lot of experienced owners are in our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.

Hal
